title: ReplicaSets, StatefulSets & DaemonSets
intro: Deployments aren't the only thing that manages pods for you. Let's look at the other controllers and when you'd actually reach for them.

steps.prompt: List the ReplicaSets in the namespace (these are what a Deployment creates under the hood).
steps.fake_output:
NAME              DESIRED   CURRENT   READY   AGE
web-7d8f9c6b5     3         3         3       5m
steps.explanation: You rarely manage ReplicaSets directly — Deployments own them and create a new one on every rollout.
steps.why: You'd only touch a ReplicaSet directly for advanced cases like manually scaling down an old revision — normally you talk to the Deployment instead and let it manage the ReplicaSet for you.

steps.prompt: A 'db' StatefulSet gives your database stable identity and storage — check its status.
steps.explanation: Unlike a Deployment's pods, StatefulSet pods get stable, predictable names (db-0, db-1, db-2) and each keeps its own persistent storage even after a restart.
steps.why: Use a Deployment when pods are interchangeable (a stateless web server); use a StatefulSet when they're not (a database where each replica has its own disk and identity).

steps.prompt: Scale the 'db' StatefulSet down to 1 replica.
steps.explanation: Same 'scale' command as a Deployment — StatefulSets just scale pods down in reverse ordinal order (db-2 goes first, not db-0).
steps.why: It's the same 'kubectl scale' syntax as scaling a Deployment — one flag (--replicas) works across every workload type that supports scaling.

steps.prompt: Check the DaemonSet that runs a log collector on every node.
steps.fake_output:
NAME          DESIRED   CURRENT   READY   NODE SELECTOR   AGE
log-agent     3         3         3       <none>          10d
steps.explanation: A DaemonSet runs exactly one pod per node automatically — you don't set a replica count, it just tracks how many nodes exist.
steps.why: There's no 'kubectl scale daemonset' — the pod count is driven entirely by node count, which is the whole point of a DaemonSet (log/metrics agents, network plugins).
